values: Your move-in registration has been checked. Here is a list of related procedures.
Do I have to do everything on this list today? It includes items for children, but I live alone.
Ask whether every item on the related-procedure list is required and explain that you live alone. Say it in Japanese.
Not everyone needs to complete every item. We will check according to your circumstances.
Understood. I have no children. I work for a company, but I am still checking with them about insurance.
Explain that you have no children, are employed, and have not yet received an answer about insurance. Say it in Japanese.
Let's check your insurance situation at the relevant counter. Please tell them your company has not answered yet.
I won't say that I have already decided which insurance to enroll in. Is there anything else I should check today?
Ask which items are necessary, explaining that your insurance enrollment is undecided. Say it in Japanese.
I will tell the staff what you have just explained and sort out the procedures that apply.
Please do. I would like to mark the completed move-in registration separately from the insurance that is still being checked.
Ask to record the completed move-in registration separately from the pending insurance check. Say it in Japanese.
You may leave your own notes on the list. Please do not mark unchecked items as completed.
I have noted that the move-in registration is complete and the insurance is being checked. I will take this list and check only the applicable items with the staff.
Use the list showing each item's status to check the applicable procedures. Say it in Japanese.
I will take you to the insurance staff now. I will also tell them you are awaiting your company's response.
Are you changing your appointment? May I ask your consultation date?
I am not changing the consultation date. The person accompanying me will be a friend instead of a family member, and I want to let you know.
Correct the misunderstanding: the appointment stays the same and only your companion changes. Say it in Japanese.
So the companion is changing, rather than the date or time. Will your friend also interpret?
They will help with words I don't understand. However, I want explanations about tests and such to be given directly to me.
Explain that your friend will assist with interpreting and that you want explanations yourself. Say it in Japanese.
We will explain things to you directly. We can also check at the time what information we may share with your companion.
Thank you. Previously, my family member spoke for me about everything, but this time I want you to ask me the questions.
Ask for questions to be directed to you instead of having your family take the lead as before. Say it in Japanese.
I will record that preference. Will your friend arrive at the same time?
They will arrive a little later. I am not asking you to hold up the consultation until my friend arrives. If necessary, I will discuss it when explanations are given.
Explain that your friend will arrive late and that you are not asking to stop the consultation. Say it in Japanese.
Understood. Please tell reception on the day about joining up when your friend arrives late.
The date and time stay the same, I will receive the explanations myself, and my friend will arrive later to help interpret. I will ask reception on the day how we can meet up.
Confirm the unchanged appointment, your own consultation, and arranging to meet your friend on the day. Say it in Japanese.
I have shared that information. Your consultation booking has not changed, so please come at the scheduled date and time.
You are here about a missing bicycle, correct? Do you have the key?
I have the key I use. But the spare key is not at home, so someone may have taken it out.
Explain that you have your usual key and suspect someone took the spare because its whereabouts are unknown. Say it in Japanese.
We will distinguish the missing spare key from whether someone took it out.
You're right. I didn't see anyone taking it. May I ask my family where it is kept?
Acknowledge that you did not witness it being taken and ask to contact your family. Say it in Japanese.
Of course. Please also record where and when you parked the bicycle.
My family has replied. The spare key was in a family member's drawer. I parked the bicycle at the bicycle parking area in front of the station at eight last night.
Correct the spare key's whereabouts after checking with family, and give the parking date, time, and place. Say it in Japanese.
So the spare key's whereabouts have been confirmed. Has the bicycle also been found?
The bicycle is still missing. I do not intend to cancel my missing-bicycle inquiry just because the key was found.
Distinguish finding the key from the still-missing bicycle and say you want to continue the inquiry. Say it in Japanese.
Understood. I will correct the key information and ask about the parking location and bicycle.
I withdraw my statement that a stranger has the spare key. Since the bicycle is missing, I will use the registration documents and parking record for this inquiry.
Withdraw your suspicion that a third party took the key and report using registration and parking records. Say it in Japanese.
I have corrected the record to say your family keeps the spare key. I will refer the missing-bicycle matter to the staff with the station parking record and registration documents.
Is this about the item you just mailed? Do you have the receipt?
Yes. After mailing it, I noticed that one sheet I was supposed to enclose was still in my bag. Can I get the envelope back and put it in?
Ask about an omitted enclosure discovered after mailing and retrieving the envelope. Say it in Japanese.
We need to check the situation to see whether retrieval is possible after acceptance. Let me see your receipt.
Please do. I must not take it out of the mailing box myself, right? I haven't touched it since.
Ask the staff to check without touching the collection box yourself. Say it in Japanese.
Correct. A staff member will check. Can the missing document be sent separately to the recipient?
I haven't asked yet. Rather than relying only on retrieval, I want to contact the recipient about the missing enclosure.
Say you have not checked with the recipient and choose to contact them as an alternative. Say it in Japanese.
Please go ahead with that contact too. We are checking about retrieval now.
I was able to ask the company. They want me to send it separately with a note identifying it as part of the original application.
Report the company's instructions to mail it separately with a linking note. Say it in Japanese.
If you send it separately, we will check the address and contents before accepting it. We will also tell you the result of checking the first mailing.
I will prepare a separate mailing as instructed by the company. I won't assume the first envelope can definitely be retrieved; I will keep the receipts and track both mailings.
Prepare the separate mailing and manage both receipts without requesting guaranteed retrieval. Say it in Japanese.
We will finish checking the first item and then explain how to send the separate mailing.
You are applying for a new account, correct? Do you have all the items we told you to bring?
I have identification, but no personal seal. Overseas, I only needed a signature, so I hadn't thought about it.
Explain that you have identification but no seal, and that you used signatures overseas. Say it in Japanese.
We will check what is needed for this application and what methods we can offer.
Thank you. I want to hear your guidance rather than filling it in on my own assumption that a signature is acceptable.
Request an explanation of the method for this application without assuming a signature is allowed. Say it in Japanese.
For this application at the counter, these are the items to bring. Other application methods have conditions too.
My company has asked me to open the account today, but I will not force the process through with missing items. May I take the guidance home?
Prioritize obtaining missing items over your company's same-day request, and ask to take the guidance home. Say it in Japanese.
Yes, you may. Please consult us after preparing the required items.
I will tell my company it was not completed today. Before coming tomorrow, I want to check every item in the guidance.
Tell your company it is unfinished and check the requirements before returning. Say it in Japanese.
There may be additional checks depending on your circumstances, so let's record what you brought today.
Please look at the documents I brought today, and I will note what is missing. Tomorrow, after preparing everything, I will consult you again about applying.
Separate what you brought from what is missing, and consult again tomorrow after preparing. Say it in Japanese.
Let's go through the checklist together. Your account will not be treated as opened today.
We are replacing the price labels. Do you have a question about a product?
I can see two prices on the same shelf. Before paying, I want to check which would apply if I buy it now.
Ask which of the two prices applies during label replacement, before paying. Say it in Japanese.
I will check the product type and which item the label covers. This is the one you selected, correct?
Yes, this one bag. I saw the cheaper label below, but it may be for the product next to it.
Show the selected size or type and acknowledge the lower price may be for another product. Say it in Japanese.
That label is for the adjacent size. This product is covered by the label we are replacing now.
Understood. I won't insist that the cheaper price must apply. Please tell me the current price.
Avoid making an incorrect claim and ask for this item's price. Say it in Japanese.
This is its price. After fixing the display, I will check that the register price matches too.
It is over my budget, so I won't take this bag. Is the smaller quantity next to it covered by the label below?
Since it exceeds your budget, check the applicable price for the smaller quantity. Say it in Japanese.
The product numbers match. Please check this smaller-quantity product.
I have checked the number and price. I will switch to the smaller quantity and put the first bag back.
Switch to the smaller item whose number and price match. Say it in Japanese.
We will proceed with that one. We will correct the confusing display on the sales floor.
We are starting to announce that the park will close soon. Do you know your way back?
I wanted to see one more place, but I need time to return to my car too. There seem to be two parking lots, and I am unsure which one.
Ask about closing time and your uncertainty between two parking lots. Say it in Japanese.
Do you remember any landmark from when you parked?
There was a large information board beside the entrance. That alone doesn't tell us which one, does it?
Explain that an information board common to both entrances is an uncertain landmark. Say it in Japanese.
Both have information boards. Do you have a photo of the entrance name or a parking ticket?
I have a photo of the entrance. Its name is visible here. It is different from the parking lot nearest us now.
Identify your parking lot from the entrance photo. Say it in Japanese.
Take this park path back there. Considering the time until closing, please head straight back.
Understood. I'll go back to the car without visiting the other place. My friend is waiting in the car too, so I'll contact them and make sure I don't get back late.
Give up further sightseeing, go straight to the car, and contact your waiting friend. Say it in Japanese.
Check the entrance name again at this fork.
I will follow the signs at the fork back to the entrance in the photo. I have told my friend I am going straight there now.
Recheck the actual entrance using the fork's signs and return. Say it in Japanese.
Please continue that way. See the rest next time when you have more time.
Do you need transfer directions? Where are you going?
I am heading toward Tokyo, and my friend is going the opposite way toward Takasaki. I thought we could take the same train part of the way.
Explain that the two of you have different destinations. Say it in Japanese.
Yes, you can take the same train to the next transfer station. You will split up after that.
So we both get off at the next station. After getting off, should we just go to opposite sides of the same platform?
Confirm in Japanese that both of you should get off at the next station, and ask whether you should then go to opposite sides of the same platform.
No. For Tokyo, cross the overhead connecting passage. For Takasaki, check the signs on the platform where you get off.
Then if my friend follows me across the passage too, they will end up going in the wrong direction.
Confirm in Japanese that if your friend follows you across the connecting passage, they will go in the wrong direction.
That's right. It will be easier if you check both routes in front of the stairs in the middle of the platform before splitting up.
We will part there. I will go up the stairs, and my friend will stay on the platform and check the signs for Takasaki.
Decide where to split up. Say it in Japanese.
Yes. Platform numbers may change according to the day's announcements, so also check the direction and destination.
My friend and I will each check our own destination before boarding, rather than checking only the number.
Explain the procedure for each person to check the signs. Say it in Japanese.
Please follow that procedure. First, both of you should take this train to the next transfer station.
Which certificate would you like?
My company told me to bring proof of my address. But I have not asked for the document's official name.
Explain what the organization receiving it requested. Say it in Japanese.
We cannot determine the type from just “proof of address.” Do you have instructions from your company?
They only told me verbally. May I phone the company now to check?
Say in Japanese that the request was only given verbally, and ask whether you may call your company now to check.
Of course. Check the name of the required certificate and the details they want included.
I should also ask whether it should show only my information or include my family too, right?
Ask in Japanese whether you should also check with your company if the document should show only your information or include your family as well.
Yes. Once you know the recipient's requirements, we can guide you through an application here based on them.
The person in charge is away from their desk, and I am told the answer will come this afternoon. I would like to wait without submitting an application form now.
Say in Japanese that the person responsible is away and the answer will come this afternoon. Explain that you would like to wait without submitting the application form now.
Understood. Once you receive the answer, compare the official name with this guide.
I will return after noting the name and required details. I won't choose based only on the phrase “proof of address.”
Say you will apply after finding out the name. Say it in Japanese.
Yes. We will give you the guide today. Please return to the counter once you have confirmed it.
You wrote “today” in the “since when” section of the medical questionnaire.
Today is when it became distressing. Should I also write when I first began to notice it a little?
Clarify the question about the starting time. Say it in Japanese.
Yes. Please make clear when you first noticed it and how it changed afterward.
I first noticed it in the evening three days ago. It only bothered me a little then, but it has felt much worse since this morning.
Say which day you first noticed it. Say it in Japanese.
So it began in the evening three days ago and became stronger this morning. Do you remember the exact time?
Three days ago it was after I got home, so I think around six. I do not remember the exact time.
Say in Japanese that it was after you got home three days ago, so you think it was around six, but you do not remember the exact time.
Writing “around the evening” is fine. Do not force yourself to specify something you don't remember.
Then I will change it to “since the evening three days ago; became stronger this morning.”
Say in Japanese that you will revise the questionnaire to show both time points: it started in the evening three days ago and became stronger this morning.
Yes. Please tell the doctor in that order too.
I have corrected it. This makes it clear that it did not suddenly start only today, doesn't it?
Say in Japanese that you have corrected the questionnaire, and check whether it now makes clear that the problem did not suddenly begin today.
Thank you. We will take your recorded history and pass it to the person handling your consultation.
reason: Repair confirmed English/Vietnamese naturalness and hint-clarity defects after complete scenario-context review; preserve all remaining source meaning and merge corrected canonical hints.
